newsitem.title: USA: SW Kansas wheat damage seen at 30-40 percent -tour.
newsitem.headline: SW Kansas wheat damage seen at 30-40 percent -tour.

text.p: Crop scouts on the second day of the Wheat Quality Council's annual hard red winter wheat tour put preliminary freeze damage estimates from six southwest Kansas counties at 30 to 40 percent.

"We had 30 to 40 percent damage and I foresee some problems increase as the season progresses," said Merle Koehn, operations manager for Grain Growers Coop in Montezuma. "But there is potential out there. It isn't a write-off."
Koehn said one problem to watch was potential lodging of the wheat plants since stems were weakened by the freezing temperatures which clamped down on the area April 11-12.
Tour participants surveyed six counties in southwest Kansas, including Morton, Stevens, Meade, and Gray counties.
Scouts said they detected Russian leaf aphid infestation in Stevens, Meade and Gray counties. The small, black insects sap nutrients from developing plants.

Scouts estimated that production potential before the April freeze, based on tiller counts, was 30 to 50 bushels per acre in the six counties surveyed. But yields were expected to be cut by 30 to 40 percent following the cold snap.
Most plants were in the boot stage of development and many fields were in the early heading stage.
The tour wraps up on Thursday at the Kansas City Board of Trade. Roughly 60 participants have been scouting Kansas and Nebraska fields since Tuesday.
